OSPF_TC88.title: Verify that SonicWALL doesn't send any OSPF packets when the OSPF feature is disabled.
OSPF_TC88.result: in step 4, after disable OSPF on sonicwall, it must not send any OSPF messages.

Interval_TC89.steps:
1. Configure OSPF for the 172.30.30.2/24 network on the Cisco router that is connected to the hub
1. Configure OSPF for the 192.168.200.2/24 network on the Cisco router that is connected to the hub2.
2. On the Network>Routing page of the SonicWALL, select Advanced Routing in the Routing Mode drop-down. Click OK in the message.
3. Configure OSPF for X0 (LAN) and X2 (DMZ) interfaces. Select the following: OSPFv2:Enabled, Area:0, Area Type:Normal, Router ID:10.0.0.
Have a Hello Interval set to 10 seconds. Capture OSPF packets on LAN and DMZ using Ethereal.
4. Edit OSPF for X0. Change Hello Interval to 25 seconds. Capture OSPF packets on sonicwall.
Interval_TC89.title: Verify that Hello packets are sent every Hello Interval seconds to the IP multicast address (224.0.0.5).
Interval_TC89.result:
in step 3, Verify that at step3 SonicWALL sends Hello packets from 192.168.200.1 and 172.30.30.1 interfaces every 10 seconds.
in step 4, At step4 SonicWALL sends Hello packets every 25 seconds.

Declare_TC90.title: Verify that SonicWALL doesn't declare a DR or DBR in its Hello packets before the Wait timer reaches Dead Interval.
Declare_TC90.result: in step 4, sonicwall won't declare DR or BDR untill the timer reaches Dead Interval.

DeadInterval_TC91.title: Verify that disabled router disappears from SonicWALLs neighbour list after Dead Interval expires
DeadInterval_TC91.result:
in step 3, the OSPF neighbor list include router in sonicwall;
in step 4, disable OSPF on router, wait about 40 seconds, which is the dead interval, the router disappeared on neighbor list in sonicwall.

RouterPrior_TC93.title: Verify that if a Router Priority is set to 0, the SonicWALL is not eligible to become a DR.
RouterPrior_TC93.result:
in step 6, sonicwall must not declare itself as DR or BDR in the hello message it transmits to neighbor router; in step 7, as there is no DR or BDR, sonicwall and router can not reach to FULL state, the OSPF status between them will stay in 2-Way.
e.g.
OSPF process 0:
Neighbor ID Pri State Dead Time Address Interface
28.1.1.55 0 2-Way/DROther 00:00:40 28.1.1.55 X3

HelloMismatch_TC96.title: Verify that the Hello packet is dropped and a sender is not accepted as a neighbor if there is Hello mismatch.
HelloMismatch_TC96.result:
in step 6, sonicwall received mismatch hello message from router, but it does not accept router as its active neighbor in its hello message;
in step 7, the neighbor list is blank on sonicwall.

DiffIP_TC97.title: Verify that if an incoming OSPF packet is not from a local network, SonicWALL should not list a sender as a neighbor in its Hello packets.
DiffIP_TC97.result:
in step 5, when sonicwall received hello packets from 55.1.1.1, it does not add this router into its active neighbor list in its own hello message;
in step 6, the neighbor list is blank on sonicwall.

EBit_TC98.title: Verify that the E bit of the Options field in a Hello packet is set if the attached area is not a stub area.
EBit_TC98.result:
in step 4, when the area type is normal, the E bit of option field in Hello packet must be set;
in step 5, when the area type is stub, the E bit must be cleared.

MasterSlave_TC101.title: Verify that Master/Slave is properly negotiated if SonicWALL has a lower Router ID than the other router.
MasterSlave_TC101.result:
in step 3, sonicwall and router exchange the DB Description message with different DD sequence number and both of them set the M/S bit to 1;
in step 4, the sonicwall with lower router-id send the second DB Description , respond to router's DB Description with router's DD sequence number, and set the M/S bit to 0, it means router becomes master and sonicwall becomes slave;

MasterSlave_TC102.title: Verify that Master/Slave is properly negotiated if SonicWALL has a higher Router ID than the other router.
MasterSlave_TC102.result:
in step 3, sonicwall and router exchange the DB Description message with different DD sequence number and both of them set the M/S bit to 1;
in step 4, the router with lower router-id send the second DB Description , respond to sonicwall's DB Description with sonicwall's DD sequence number, and set the M/S bit to 0, it means sonicwall becomes master and other router becomes slave;

VPN_TC152.title: AO Group used in site to site VPN

NSM_TC153.steps:
Establishe ospf between DUT and peer router, and enable restribute static route in DUT
2. Add a static route, destination 81.1.1.0/24, interface X1, gw X1 default gateway, check DUT nsm and peer router
3. Change destination by select another AO(network/host) in Routing page, check DUT nsm and peer router
4. Change destination by edit AO(network/netmask) in AO page, check DUT nsm and peer router
5. Repeat step3~5 for change gateway AO, check DUT nsm and peer router
6. Change the interface, check DUT nsm and peer router
Note, make sure the static route is active in nsm, inactive route can't be redistribute to router
NSM_TC153.title: Verify the PBR's parameter(gateway/destination/interface) changes can be updated to nsm and can be restributed to the neighbor
NSM_TC153.result:
in step2, 81.1.1.0 should be shown in DUT nsm and peer router routing table
in step3,4,5,6, the updated route show in DUT nsm and peer router.
